title: Countable and uncountable nouns
subtitle: Singular, plural, a few, a little, and nouns that change meaning

blocks.text: Countable nouns have a singular and a plural form and take a singular or plural verb.

rows.example: There are over 100 **shops** in the new shopping centre.
They've got some great toys for **babies** in there.
We need to get some new **dishes** for this evening.

blocks.intro: We use these words with countable nouns:

blocks.text: A few countable nouns have irregular plurals.
blocks.note: one child, two **children** · one foot, two **feet** · one man, two **men** · one person, two **people** · one tooth, two **teeth** · one woman, two **women**

blocks.text: We cannot count some nouns (uncountable nouns). They do not have a plural form and take a singular verb, even if they end in **-s**.

items: We can use **any** in questions and negative statements with both countable nouns and plural countable nouns:

blocks.text: There are a few uncountable nouns that are plural and are followed by a plural verb. Be careful with **clothes** and **jeans**.

blocks.correct: Your clean **clothes are** on the bed.
blocks.incorrect: Your clean **clothes is** on the bed.

blocks.text: Some nouns are uncountable with one meaning and countable with another meaning.
blocks.note: Get me some **paper** when you go to the shops. (= a packet of paper to write on) · Get me **a paper** when you go to the shops. (= a newspaper)

exercises.title: A · Irregular plurals
exercises.instruction: Complete using the plural form of a word from the box.

items.prompt: Did you know that Jason's dog has had three beautiful ___ ?
The Spice Girls was an all-girl band, so there weren't any ___ .
It's a bit strange that Victor wears two ___ — one on each arm.
If ___ do the same jobs as their husbands, they should be paid the same.
The dentist says I have to have two ___ taken out!
How many ___ were there at the show?
We've walked miles! My ___ are hurting!
Mrs Jenkins has just had a baby, so she's got three ___ now.

exercises.title: B · Circle the correct word
exercises.instruction: Select the form that agrees with the noun.

items.prompt: Your money ___ on the table in the dining room.
The advice you gave me ___ really useful. Thanks!

There ___ been a lot of bad news recently.
Your homework ___ late. Please do it sooner next time.
___ the information about the museum include the opening times?
We need new furniture in the dining room. ___ very old and scratched.
The fish in this tank all ___ to be ill.
I love your hair. ___ really soft.

exercises.title: D · Similar meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given. Write no more than three words.

items.prompt: We don't know anything about the problem. **information** — We don't ___ about the problem.
acceptedAnswers: We don't have any information about the problem.

items.prompt: Is it okay if I have some cheese? **bit** — Is it okay if I have ___ cheese?
acceptedAnswers: Is it okay if I have a bit of cheese?

items.prompt: There's only a little coffee left in the jar. **much** — There ___ coffee left in the jar.
acceptedAnswers: There isn't much coffee left in the jar.

items.prompt: I try not to drink too much Coca-Cola in a week. **cans** — I try not to drink too ___ of Coca-Cola in a week.
acceptedAnswers: I try not to drink too many cans of Coca-Cola in a week.

items.prompt: Would you like some more chocolate? **piece** — Would you like ___ chocolate?
acceptedAnswers: Would you like another piece of chocolate?

items.prompt: I don't want a lot of cream on my strawberries. **cream** — I only want ___ on my strawberries.
acceptedAnswers: I only want a little cream on my strawberries.

exercises.title: E · Choose the correct answer
exercises.instruction: Select the meaning that fits the sentence.

items.prompt: Be careful with that vase because it's made of ___ !
I started coughing because I had ___ at the back of my throat.
Don't put your hot cup on my new table! It's ___ and I don't want you to burn it.
We should all recycle ___ so that it can be used again.
My dad gets ___ every day on his way to work.
Of course you can have some milk. Get ___ out of the cupboard.

exercises.title: F · Open-air markets
exercises.instruction: Write one word in each gap.

items.prompt: Even if you only have a ___ money, you can still have a great time at your local open-air market.
The clothes ___ cheap,
and the fruit ___ cheap, too!
Often, the food in your local supermarket ___ travelled a long way,
but at the market you know that you're buying food which has been produced locally. The vegetables ___ fresh,
even if you go late in the day when there are only a ___ left.
Support your local market and help local farmers. Contact your Town Hall to find out if there are ___ open-air markets in your area.
